CheckTitle: KV namespaces storing sensitive data should have key-sanitisation verified
Description: Inventories KV namespaces and flags those whose title suggests they store sensitive or user-scoped data (sessions, auth tokens, cache entries keyed by user ID). Workers that use user-controlled KV keys without sanitisation can leak data between users.
Risk: If a Worker uses user-supplied input as KV keys without validation, an attacker can enumerate or overwrite other users' data. KV has no built-in access control per key — it relies entirely on the Worker logic.

Code.Other: Audit the Worker code that uses this KV namespace to ensure user-supplied key components are namespaced (e.g. prefix with user ID hash) and that Workers do not expose raw KV key enumeration to external callers.

Recommendation.Text: Namespace KV keys by user identifier (e.g. 'user:{userId}:session:{sessionId}') to prevent cross-user access. Never allow user-supplied strings to directly form complete KV keys without sanitisation.

Notes: This is a naming-convention heuristic. Namespaces matching 'session', 'auth', 'token', 'user', 'cache', 'public', 'secret', or 'credential' are flagged for manual review.
